title: How a Man Becomes Wise We are living in the golden age of information
author: Chris Martin
source: The Ways of a Gentleman (Martin Substack), January 21, 2026
summary: Martin contends that access to information does not equal wisdom—we live in an age of unprecedented information abundance yet declining wisdom. Wisdom is different from knowledge: it involves understanding not just facts but their implications, recognizing patterns, and developing good judgment forged through experience and reflection. Martin argues that a man becomes wise by studying the examples of great men and women across history, by reading deeply rather than skimming, by listening to those with more experience and maturity, and most importantly by learning from his own mistakes and the consequences of poor choices. Wisdom requires humility—the recognition that one does not already know everything and that growth comes from paying attention to the world and others' counsel. A wise man learns continuously throughout his life.
points: Access to information does not equal wisdom—we live in unprecedented information abundance yet declining wisdom because wisdom requires judgment, not just facts.
Wisdom is forged through experience, reflection, and learning from mistakes—it cannot be downloaded or acquired quickly but must be built through a lifetime of attention.
A man becomes wise by studying great examples, reading deeply, listening to those with maturity and experience, and humbling himself to learn from others.
Wisdom requires intellectual humility—the recognition that one does not already know everything and that growth comes from continued learning.
The wise man is a lifelong learner who pays attention to the world, reads history, listens to counsel, and reflects on both his successes and failures.
quotes: We are living in the golden age of information. Access to knowledge is easier than ever before in human history. Yet wisdom seems to be declining, not increasing.
Wisdom is different from knowledge. Knowledge is having facts and information. Wisdom is understanding what those facts mean and what to do with them.
A man becomes wise by studying the examples of great men and women across history, reading deeply rather than skimming, and listening to those with more experience and maturity.
Most importantly, wisdom comes from learning from one's own mistakes and the consequences of poor choices through careful reflection.
Wisdom requires humility—the recognition that one does not already know everything and that growth comes from paying attention to the world and others' counsel.

A wise man learns continuously throughout his life, understanding that wisdom is not a destination but a never-ending pursuit of understanding and good judgment.” Archived from The Ways of a Gentleman (Martin Substack) on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
